content.title: About
content.content: Hayacas are a traditional Puerto Rican bread roll made from wheat flour, sugar, butter, eggs, and yeast. The dough is slightly sweet, soft, and airy, with a golden crust on the outside. Hayacas are commonly served for breakfast, lunch, or as a snack, and can be paired with cheese, ham, or sweet fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hayacas appeared in Puerto Rico in the early 20th century under American culinary influence.
Traditionally the rolls are baked as small round buns, but they are also shaped into “pancakes” for special occasions.
The original recipe uses milk, giving the crumb a more tender texture than ordinary bread.
Hayacas are often served with “avocado mash” or a sweet cinnamon‑sugar glaze called “moco”.
Puerto Rico celebrates “Hayaca Day”, when hundreds of rolls are baked for charitable events.

items.title: Carbohydrate source
items.content: Hayacas provide a quick source of energy thanks to their mix of simple and complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the recipe add a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour and yeast are rich in B1, B2, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Milk and butter supply calcium and phosphorus, important for bone health.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Traditional recipes use salt sparingly, making the roll suitable for moderate sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Hayacas contain wheat flour and are not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugar makes the product calorie‑dense; those monitoring blood sugar should limit portions.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Milk and butter may cause issues for individuals with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, the roll is relatively high in calories; moderation is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hayacas can be eaten fresh, lightly toasted, with butter, jam, cheese, or ham. They are often sliced in half and used as sandwich bases. In sweet versions, the rolls are drizzled with cinnamon‑sugar glaze.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store hayacas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator (up to 7 days) or freeze in a sealed bag for up to 3 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.
